title: Concurrent Distance-Learning Certifications and the Rate of Pursuit
content:
Under Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education), a student may hold a resident term certification and, alongside it, a certification whose courses are all distance learning. The concurrent distance-learning certification is the latest certification on the benefit whose courses are all distance learning; its credits enter the rate of pursuit confirmed on a monthly verification as follows.

**Rule.** Credits of the concurrent distance-learning certification are added according to how its term sits against the resident term:
- when its term lies wholly inside the resident term (starting on or after the resident term start and ending on or before the resident term end), all of its credits are added;
- when its term only partly overlaps the resident term, its credits are added in proportion to the days of its term that fall inside the resident term, counting the overlapping days with both ends included over the days of its term with both ends included;
- when its term does not overlap the resident term, or there is no such certification, nothing is added.

**How the added credits enter the rate.** The credits added are divided by the full-time measure of the distance-learning term and joined to the resident credits counted divided by the resident term's full-time measure; that sum is multiplied by 100 once, rounded half up to a whole percent only at that final step, and never set above 100 percent.

**Positive and negative cases (hypothetical dates and credits)**

| Distance-learning term against the resident term | Its credits | Credits added |
|---|---|---|
| 56-day term wholly inside the resident term | 6 | 6 |
| 56-day term, 28 of its days inside the resident term | 6 | 6 times 28 divided by 56: 3 |
| 56-day term, 14 of its days inside the resident term | 6 | 6 times 14 divided by 56: 1.5 |
| Term ending the day before the resident term starts | 6 | None |
| No distance-learning certification on the benefit | — | None |

*Hypothetical assembly:* resident credits counted 9 against a measure of 12 (0.75) and 3 distance-learning credits added against a measure of 6 (0.5) give 1.25; times 100 is 125, and the rate confirmed is 100 percent.
